profile.headline: Software Engineer
profile.summary:
Chris loves robots, dinosaurs, and most things sugary. He loves system/architectural design problems in interviews or as thought experiments. Most of his experience is in mobile application development, especially in the Android world. Chris enjoys developing in C++ and Java.

In his recent spare time, he's been slowly learning how to develop video games. He hopes to expand his knowledge of ROS and embedded systems in the near future.

Chris is very interested in STEM outreach programs.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
- Formalized plan to refactor system architecture for map visualization and customization.
- Instituted team transition to Rx/Observables in conjunction with ViewModel UI patterns in C++.
- Engineered a system to display standardized content with streamlined development.
- Implemented transition to Android App Bundles for improved app modularization and resource management.
- Launched j7+ with support for "Obstacle Image Review", a user-based classification system.
- Facilitated cross-functional team coordination as Scrum Master, team lead, and release engineer.
- Coordinated CI/CD system transition with continued pipeline and build improvements.
- Orchestrated app codebase transition to C++17.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
- Spearheaded refactoring effort to standardize and simplify interpretation of robot state data in the app.
- Refined monolithic data classes to use observable patterns for integration with model-view-presenter.
- Launched i7+, s9+, and m6 with ability to create schedules utilizing rooms in the home from the app.
- Integrated app with Clean Base to track dirt evacuation status and manual initiation through MQTT.
- Updated Android NDK dependencies across team for improved C++ support.
- Implemented iRobot Beta and Cleaning Preferences UI for the Android app.
- Collaborated with hardware, cloud, UX, and testing teams in stand-ups, planning, and retrospectives for scrum processes.

positions.title: Teaching Assistant
positions.description:
ITP 165: Introduction to C++
Guided students'​ understanding of the fundamentals of C++ in office hours and labs. Led off-hours discussion and Q/A sessions using Piazza.

ACAD 276: Introduction to Coding and Application Development
Supported learning of simple Android development with examples and demos of tools and libraries such as Genymotion, Volley, and Glide. Exceeded 60% attendance during optional Sunday office hours.

ITP 341: Application Development for Phone and Tablet
Established head TA role focusing on creating new content and managing student Q/A on Piazza. Accelerated course by over 15% with live demos and new content including lectures on Fragments, Relative Layout, View Pagers, and cloud databases. Introduced assignments emphasizing UI/UX.

positions.title: Software Engineering Intern
positions.description:
Developed for the 2016 update of the NFL Sunday Ticket app for Android.

-	Confirmed similar battery and network performance relative to YouTube streaming using Battery Historian.
-	Resolved fatal dynamic permission soft-lock involving Location services for Android Marshmallow onwards.
-	Presented robust custom views depicting player statistics and images obtained from internal REST API.
-	Scripted visualization from Google Play Developer Console for comparison of ratings between builds.

projects.title: Long Journey
projects.description:
Encounter monsters as you journey throughout the day on your Android Wear (watch).

This is a project I work on alone. The idea was to encourage exercising while engaging the user, unlike the more passive exercise companion apps on the market. This underwent hiatus for the Android Wear 2.0 release and massive overhaul as a result. With the changes introduced in Nougat and Oreo, this project may be hard to revive using stock Android.

-	Engaged users by offering options in each encounter then seamlessly transitioning notifications into the app.
-	Conceptualized user retention with increased walk cycles, equipment system, and intuitive fatigue system.
-	Catalogued necessary changes to adapt app to Android Wear 2.0 standard and avoid deprecation.

projects.title: World Planner
projects.description:
Expand your story world by detailing characters, their interactions, locations, significant items, and more on Android.

This was a project I undertook as a "commission" from my sister. I work on it intermittently alone.

-	Monitored beta testing, crash reporting, and engagement through Crashlytics and Answers from Fabric.
-	Devised persistent storage of content and camera-captured images using SugarORM (through SQLite).
-	Designed with Material Design standards including Bottom Navigation, and Floating Action Buttons.
